article.Citation/Title: Smith, C. M. (1958). A new adjunct to the treatment of alcoholism: The hallucinogenic drugs. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 19, 406-417.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Smith, C. M. (1958). A new adjunct to the treatment of alcoholism The hallucinogenic drugs.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Single oral dose LSD (200-400 mcg) or mescaline (0.5g) in hospital; prolonged interview during session, discussed drinking problems, discharged days later; A.A. follow-up.

ae_events.Description: In-session psychological/perceptual disturbance (anxiety, perceptual distortion) of variable intensity, author-classified mild/moderate/intense
Transient nausea occurring 30 minutes to 2 hours after drug administration
Vomiting, explicitly noted as not severe
Severe in-session anxiety and persisting depression (Case 17) requiring sodium seconal sedation
Mild liver function test abnormalities noted in some patients under the Side Effects heading

article.Outcome: No test statistic is reported anywhere in the article; treatment response is reported only as counts in three ordered clinical categories (Table 1/Table 2 and Summary): 6 much improved, 6 improved, 12 unchanged, 0 worse, out of 24. This is the article's sole, stated primary outcome (drinking response) with no comparator, so it is coded as a single-arm improvement rate: 12/24 (50%) improved or better.
article.SD: No dispersion measure or test statistic (SD, SE, F, t, chi-squared) is reported anywhere for the treatment-response outcome; the article is purely descriptive/tabular.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: All 24 enrolled patients were followed up ('A follow-up investigation was carried out on all the patients') and all 24 appear in the Table 1/Table 2 results, so N analyzed = N enrolled = 24.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, design (single-dose LSD/mescaline adjunct pilot), setting (University Hospital, Saskatoon), sample selection ('most difficult cases', A.A. failures), intervention (dose/route/session structure), outcome categories, results (Tables 1-2, case vignettes), side effects, and funding (National Health Grants, Rockefeller Foundation) are all explicitly described. There is no comparator group, no sample-size or power justification, and randomization/blinding/statistical methods are never mentioned at all (not even as absent) because the design is single-arm and purely descriptive with no significance testing. 9/14 met, below the 13-of-14 threshold for MethodologyDescribedYN = 1.

article.EligibleYN: Criterion (a): 24 patients received a prospectively assigned single-dose LSD/mescaline regimen under a defined study protocol (Methods section) with prospective follow-up (2 months-3 years) — a single-arm open-label clinical trial per the eligibility boundary case. Criterion (b): the stated outcome is drinking behavior (abstinence/reduction/unchanged), a direct substance-use endpoint. Both criteria met.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 1 to match the EligibleYN=Y criterion-(a) judgment: a prospectively planned single-dose intervention with defined enrollment and prospective outcome assessment.
article.Pos Result Y/N: No comparator exists, so directionality is judged from the study's own pre/post framing: 12/24 (50%) rated much improved or improved, none worsened, and the authors describe the results as 'sufficiently encouraging to merit more extensive... trials.' Coded 1 (positive) rather than 3, since the direction is stated, not ambiguous, even though the effect is modest and confined mainly to the character-disorder subgroup.
article.RandomizationYN: Single-arm, open-label pilot with no randomization procedure described anywhere; coded 0 per the v1.2 single-arm rule, not 3.
article.BlindingYN: No blinding of any kind is described (open interview, unblinded drug administration); coded 0 per the v1.2 single-arm rule.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 0 to remain consistent with BlindingYN = 0 (cannot be 1 when BlindingYN = 0).
article.Comparator: No control, placebo, or active-comparator group; all 24 patients received LSD or mescaline. Coded 0 per the v1.2 single-arm rule, not 3.
article.PrimaryCare: All care occurred in an inpatient psychiatric/university hospital research setting with follow-up through Alcoholics Anonymous and a provincial alcoholism bureau; no interface with primary-care providers or settings is described.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power discussion of any kind appears; the article is explicitly framed as a preliminary/pilot study without any sample-size justification.
article.Retention (%): Not randomized, so the denominator is the enrolled N (24). The article states follow-up was obtained on 'all the patients,' i.e., 24/24 completers = 100%.
article.MediatingYN: No formal mediation analysis (indirect-effect test, causal mediation model, Baron-and-Kenny-style regression sequence) is conducted anywhere. The Discussion narratively observes that 'those patients who had an intense reaction did better than those having a mild one' — a candidate intermediate variable (drug-reaction intensity, which is measured per-patient in Table 1) discussed as possibly explaining outcome, but with no formal test of the indirect pathway. Per the rule that a narrative 'may explain' claim with no test run is 0, not 1, and since a candidate mediator (reaction intensity) actually was measured (ruling out 3), coded 0.
article.ModeratingYN: No interaction term or formal effect-modification test is reported. Table 2 reports drinking-outcome results side by side by diagnostic category (character disorder / psychopathy / psychosis) — a candidate moderator that was measured — but this is a stratified presentation of results, not a formal moderation/interaction analysis. Per the rule that subgroup results reported side by side with no interaction test are 0, not 1, and since a candidate moderator (diagnosis) was measured (ruling out 3), coded 0.
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: The primary outcome (drinking-response classification) is reported purely descriptively throughout — as raw counts and percentages in Table 1, Table 2, and the Summary — with no p-value, no confidence interval, no named test statistic (t/F/chi-squared), and no explicit verbal significance claim ('significantly better/worse') anywhere in the article for this outcome. A primary comparison does exist (treatment response across the cohort and by diagnostic subgroup in Table 2), so this is a purely descriptive report of an existing comparison rather than the absence of any comparison to test; coded 0, not 3.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: The sample-selection basis is explicitly stated ('Only the most difficult cases were taken into this study. All but four... had tried A.A. and were considered to have failed') rather than a formal numbered list; coded 1 as a borderline but genuine statement of selection criteria.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Drinking outcome was rated by clinician judgment into three ordinal categories (much improved/improved/unchanged), not a named validated instrument; liver function tests and glucose tolerance are biochemical, not scale-based. Coded 0.
article.BaseStatus: Sample is explicitly the most refractory subgroup: mean 12.1 years of uncontrolled drinking, 8/24 with prior delirium tremens, complications in all but 2 cases, and prior A.A. failure in all but 4 — coded 'Severe'.
article.Age_Median: Ages of the 24 patients (Table 1) range 20-63; computed mean = 38.6, computed median = 36 (average of the 12th/13th sorted values), both falling in the 30-50 bracket.
article.PercentFem: 23 of 24 patients are listed 'M' and 1 (case 16) is listed 'F' in Table 1: 1/24 = 4.17%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: No race/ethnicity breakdown is reported for the cohort; only Case 17 is described incidentally as 'of Italian origin,' which is not a cohort-level race/ethnicity figure.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No explicit statement that low-SES participants were included or described at the cohort level (income, insurance status, eligibility criteria); coded 0.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted at University Hospital, Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada — coded 'NonUS'; actual location given here per instructions.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Sample was deliberately restricted to 'the most difficult cases' who had already failed A.A. — a highly selected, non-representative refractory subgroup, not a real-world community/clinical sample; coded 0.
article.InterventionTherapy: Drug administration was explicitly combined with a prolonged psychotherapeutic interview during the session, prior rapport-building psychotherapy (2-4 weeks), and post-session follow-up psychotherapy plus occupational/recreational therapy; coded 1.
article.HarmsAssessed: A dedicated 'Side Effects' section reports nausea, vomiting, and liver-function monitoring, and reaction intensity was systematically graded per patient; SafetyReported = 'Y' accordingly, so HarmsAssessed = 1.
article.Followup in months: Article states follow-up 'ranging from 2 months to 3 years' with an average of 1 year; longest reported duration (3 years) converts to 36 months.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Anxiety/depression are described qualitatively within individual case narratives and as acute drug-session phenomena, but no formal mental-health outcome or scale is reported as a study endpoint distinct from the drinking-outcome classification; coded 0.
article.MortalityMeasured: No deaths are mentioned anywhere in the article ('None of the patients followed up became worse'); mortality was not assessed or reported as an outcome, coded 0.
article.LSD: LSD-25 (200-400 gamma) was administered as one of the two study interventions (Table 1, Method section).
article.Mescaline: Mescaline (0.5 g) was administered as the other study intervention (Table 1, Method section); some patients (e.g., case 22) received both LSD and mescaline across sessions.
article.MultiplePsychedelic: Both LSD and mescaline were used as interventions across the cohort (and within-patient in at least case 22), so both substance flags are 1 and MultiplePsychedelic = 1 per the rule that it must be 1 whenever two or more substance flags are 1.
article.SafetyReported: A dedicated 'Side Effects' section plus per-patient reaction-intensity grading (Table 1) and liver-function/glucose monitoring constitute an explicit safety assessment; coded 'Y'.
article.AnyAEReported: Nausea, vomiting, variable-intensity psychological/perceptual reactions, one case requiring sedative intervention, and mild liver-function abnormalities are all reported; coded 'Y'.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Five distinct AE types were identified: (1) general in-session psychological/perceptual disturbance, (2) nausea, (3) vomiting, (4) Case 17's severe anxiety/depression requiring sodium seconal, (5) mild liver-function-test abnormalities.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: No single combined count of participants with >=1 AE is given anywhere; the article reports overlapping subsets (22/24 with a graded reaction, 3 vomited, 'many' with nausea, 'some' with LFT abnormalities) that cannot be summed into one union count, so coded '.'.
article.AE_denominator: All 24 patients received a psychedelic dose and were assessed under the Side Effects section and Table 1's reaction-intensity column, so the safety population equals the full enrolled sample of 24.
article.ArmScope: Single-arm study; every reported AE value derives solely from the psychedelic-exposed cohort, so 'psychedelic_arm' per the rule that this applies to single-arm studies by definition.
article.WorstSeverity: Maximum severity across the five ae_events entries is Moderate (Case 17's anxiety/depression requiring sodium seconal, AE04); no event met an FDA seriousness criterion or CTCAE Grade 4-5 equivalent.

ae_events.Smith 1958_AE01: Table 1 grades each patient's reaction intensity mild/moderate/intense; cases 9 and 11 are explicitly stated to have shown 'no reaction beyond some slight increase in tension,' leaving 22/24 with a graded reaction. The narrative states these effects 'persisted for an average of 8 or 9 hours' and 'in all cases, the patients felt well by the following day,' supporting a default Mild grading per the rubric's expected-acute-drug-effect principle, since no general intervention or lasting impairment is described for the cohort as a whole (Case 17's exception is captured separately as AE04).
ae_events.Smith 1958_AE03: Authors explicitly qualify vomiting as 'not severely,' which is treated as an author-assigned severity descriptor (SeveritySource = author) rather than rubric inference.
ae_events.Smith 1958_AE04: Case 17 narrative: 2 hours after LSD, 'tension and depression were so marked that sodium seconal... was administered,' with 'some relief of the tension but the depression persisted' afterward, complicating the therapeutic relationship. Graded Moderate per the rubric (active pharmacological intervention required, functional/therapeutic impairment beyond the dosing day) but not Severe, since no FDA seriousness criterion (hospitalization, life-threatening event, persistent disability) is described.
ae_events.Smith 1958_AE05: Text states 'Some of the patients showed mild abnormalities of the liver function tests' without naming how many, and discusses cases 8 and 10's pre-existing hepatic conditions (cirrhosis, prior hepatitis) in the same passage without clarifying whether the LFT abnormalities were drug-induced or pre-existing baseline findings. Severity is graded Mild per the authors' own word ('mild', SeveritySource = author), but SeverityIndeterminate = Y because the affected count and drug-attributability are both unclear.

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, open-label pilot with no comparator group and no dispersion or test statistic reported anywhere; only a categorical pre/post improvement rate (much improved/improved/unchanged) is available, which has no defensible standardized-effect-size conversion.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 50% of a deliberately refractory, A.A.-failure alcoholic sample (12/24) were rated much improved or improved on drinking outcome post-treatment, none worsened, and the authors characterize the results as sufficiently encouraging to justify further controlled trials.
